data.title: Enish Plans to Sell 5,932 SOL and Seek Withdrawal From SBI Crypto Fund I
data.description: Japanese listed gaming company Enish plans to sell all 5,932.0586 SOL it holds between November 27 and December 27 and has proposed withdrawing its 50 million yen investment in SBI Crypto Fund I. According to Foresight News, Enish bought the SOL for approximately 99.94 million yen and estimates it will incur a loss of about 43 million yen, with the actual amount depending on sale prices and fees. The withdrawal request is subject to approval by the fund operator. Enish said the moves are intended to prioritize funding for its gaming business and financial stability. It will continue its digital asset treasury business but has no specific plans to buy SOL again.

data.title: Palliser Capital Urges Chemring Breakup, Sees Up to 80% Stock Upside
data.description: According to CNBC, Palliser Capital, a top-10 Chemring shareholder with a nearly 3% stake, is urging the U.K. defense group to sell its Roke unit and use the proceeds to expand investment and manufacturing capacity. The activist investor says a strategic overhaul could lift Chemring’s valuation to between £8.34 and £9.16 per share, representing up to 80% upside over 12 months. Chemring’s countermeasures protect 85% of NATO’s air fleet and 60% of its naval fleet, according to figures from Palliser and Chemring. The company reported a record £1.4 billion order book as of Oct. 31, up from £1.3 billion a year earlier. A Chemring spokesperson said the company welcomes shareholder engagement but does not comment on media or market speculation.

data.title: Aliko Dangote's Refinery IPO Implies $47 Billion Valuation
data.description: According to CNBC, the minority-stake IPO of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE implies a valuation of about $47 billion, based on a 525-naira ($0.39) offer price and the company's registered share count, according to Reuters' calculations. The offering has reportedly been heavily oversubscribed, with investors from 120 countries and all 54 African countries applying to buy shares, the company said. The refinery is expected to begin trading in Lagos on Dec. 1, following regulatory approval, according to multiple media reports.

data.title: Ella Zhang: What YZi Labs Seeks in Early-Stage Founders
data.description:
YZi Labs said on X that YZi Labs Managing Partner and Head Ella Zhang outlined the qualities the firm looks for when backing early-stage founders during an appearance at CoinDesk Live. She cited strong early signals of product-market fit, a deep—often personal—connection to the problem, resilience through market cycles, and alignment with the investment thesis YZi Labs publishes each season through its Request for Startups.

Zhang said the firm values hearing founders explain their personal reasons for working on a problem and why it matters to them.

data.title: Binance to Move 7,500 BTC From SAFU and Add 500 Million USDC
data.description:
According to the announcement from Binance, the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an emergency insurance fund established in July 2018 to protect users’ assets, will transfer 7,500 BTC from its SAFU address to Binance’s treasury. Binance will add 500 million USDC from its treasury to SAFU.

Binance said the change is an internal reallocation, not a sale. No BTC will be sold or traded on the market, and the transfer between SAFU and Binance’s own funds will have no market impact.

The change meets a regulatory requirement, and Binance said a larger stablecoin share makes SAFU more stable and immediately usable if needed. SAFU’s purpose of protecting users in an extreme event and Binance’s commitment to replenish the fund remain unchanged.

SAFU remains held and managed by Nest Clearing and Custody Limited, an ADGM-regulated Recognised Clearing House. For more information, please refer to Binance's official announcements.

data.title: HyperLend Adds 7.25 Million HPL to Buyback
data.description: HyperLend, a lending protocol on HyperEVM, said it had added 7.25 million HPL to its buybacks. According to Foresight News, including the 5,017,336 HPL purchased over the counter in September, its cumulative buybacks have exceeded 12.25 million HPL.

data.title: DeLorean Labs to Launch Staking and Governance Protocol in December
data.description: DeLorean Labs, the Web3 division of automotive brand DeLorean, said on X that its staking and governance protocol will launch in December. According to Foresight News, the first major action after the governance protocol goes live will be a community vote proposal aimed at significantly reducing the disruptive impact of malicious actors and creating value for existing DMC token holders.

data.description: Bitdeer mined 293 BTC and sold the same amount during the week ending November 27, recording net additions of zero BTC. According to Odaily, the Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin miner holds no Bitcoin.

data.title: Arthur Hayes at Binance Blockchain Week: Overbuilt Compute Will Make AI Cheap — and Fuel a Trillion-Agent Economy
data.description:
Arthur Hayes, Chief Investment Officer of Maelstrom and co-founder of BitMEX, took the Binance Blockchain Week stage in Bangkok with a deliberately contrarian thesis: the AI trade as most investors know it is a capital incinerator — and the real bull case lies one layer below, in compute markets and agentic payments.
The Railroad Trap: Today's AI Darlings May Be Tomorrow's Bankruptcies
Hayes opened with a warning aimed squarely at traditional equity investors. History shows the companies that build transformational infrastructure rarely survive to profit from it.
In the 19th century, railroad stocks made up an estimated 50–60% of index concentration in the US and Western Europe — a level of dominance that "mirrors today where we are with AI investment companies." Yet almost nobody can name a railroad company today. The same fate met the Erie Canal, the RCA and Marconi radio stocks of the 1920s (down roughly 99%), and the fiber-optic builders of the dot-com era — Ciscos, Lucents and WorldComs.
His conclusion was blunt: the builders of AI data centers "probably won't exist in the next 5 to 10 years, or if they do, investors are down something like 90-plus percent on their money." He called recent high-profile listings including SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs "pretty much shitcoins, but in the stock market sense," predicting many neo-clouds and debt issuers would go bankrupt within 6 to 18 months.
The beneficiaries, by contrast, are the asset-light users of cheap infrastructure — "the hyperscalers of today, the Googles, the Amazons, the Facebooks" — companies not seen as internet vanguard in the 1990s but now dominant because others paid for the buildout.
The Commodity Problem: Cheap Intelligence, Worse Economics
Citing BCA Research, Hayes noted roughly 3.6% of GDP will be spent on the AI buildout — "the largest infrastructure project we've ever done in human civilization history." Hyperscaler capex alone is running at an estimated $800 billion to $1 trillion this year, with expectations of further growth.
The consequence: AI labs sell a commodity whose price keeps falling even as the cost to build capacity rises. "You don't want the price of the thing you sell to get less expensive while the cost to build the data centers gets more expensive," he said. "This is why most AI labs are terrible businesses."
But falling prices create the opportunity. Drawing a parallel with UK wheat yields and global population growth — food became cheap in the mid-20th century and the population exploded past 8 billion — Hayes argued that cheap compute begets proliferation. More compute at a lower price gives us more agents. Token spend inflects sharply from 2026, the dawn of the agentic revolution, with agents running 24/7 at the speed of light. He also cited industry expectations of roughly a 10x improvement in Nvidia chip efficiency over a decade. "If you think compute is cheap today, it's going to be much cheaper in the future."
Why Banking Rails Can't Serve Agents — and What Comes Next
Hayes turned to how billions of AI agents transact. Traditional banking, he argued, is human-centric and unfit for purpose. "How does an agent pass KYC? How does an agent process monthly invoices?" Worse, agents can be deplatformed instantly — sanctioned or blacklisted by a stablecoin issuer, losing access to funds entirely.
"Agents are computer programs built in silicon," he said. "A decentralized blockchain with a public and private key is not something that's alien to them. This is how they were built."
This is the genesis of his new project, Flop Labs, described as "food for your AI agent." The Flop Network connects agents bidding for compute with miners running consumer or enterprise-grade GPUs, and validators assembling blocks of verified inference receipts. Miners earn newly minted FLOP tokens proportional to compute contributed — tying the token directly to real work.
Hayes was candid on tokenomics abuse, noting most tokens launched in the past 24 months are down 80–95% as insiders sold and founders retired after cliffs unlocked. Flop Labs instead sold no tokens to VCs. Access comes through participation: mining, validating, or having an agent use free testnet compute. Close to 25% of the 10-year supply is being airdropped, with free compute available for 90 days and over 2 million wallets created in three to four days.
"I came out of retirement to start an AI project," Hayes said of the apparent contradiction with his bearish AI investing stance. His summary: "Overbuild AI, a bunch of companies go bankrupt, don't give a fuck. We get cheap intelligence, we get more agents, they need a system to process their payments — that's where Flop comes in."
He closed with a hypothetical CoinGecko screen showing FLOP at a $10 trillion market cap. "We can all dream," he said — but the logic is straightforward: trillions of economic agents, coordinating at the speed of light, need a currency built for machines rather than humans.

data.title: SET Chairman: Innovation and Investor Protection Are Not in Conflict — Trust Is the Foundation for Market Growth
data.description: At Binance Blockchain Week 2026, Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) Chairman Kitipong Urapeepatanapong said that “innovation and protection are not opposites. Trust is what allows innovation to scale. A market that people trust is a market that grows.”He noted that Thailand was among the earliest jurisdictions in Asia to introduce a digital asset regulatory framework in 2018, and has since developed a relatively complete licensed ecosystem covering exchanges, brokers, dealers, fund managers, advisers, and custodians.Kitipong added that clear, fair, and predictable rules are essential to attracting capital and supporting long-term digital asset market development. He also stressed that traditional finance and digital finance are not mutually exclusive, but should work together to build a broader and more efficient future capital market.

data.title: Binance Plans Bhutan Asia Hub After In-Principle Approval
data.description:
Binance Blog published a new article, reporting that Binance received in-principle approval (IPA) from the Gelephu Central Bank (GCB) to establish regulated digital-asset operations in Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC), Bhutan. The approval is not a full license; Binance must meet GCB’s conditions and complete remaining regulatory requirements before regulated activities can begin.

At Binance Blockchain Week 2026, Binance and GMC signed a cooperation agreement outlining plans for GMC to become Binance’s Asia hub. The partnership includes plans for an operational presence in Bhutan, local employment and training, and investment in talent and digital-asset capabilities.

The parties also intend to explore developing GMC as a regional center of excellence to support Binance’s broader Asia operations. SB Seker, Binance’s Head of APAC, said the location reflects the company’s commitment to operating within clear regulatory frameworks. GMC Board Director Jigdrel Singay said the partnership is intended to create jobs, develop talent and build capabilities in Bhutan.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | Global Stock Sentiment Improves as Gold and Silver Rally; Analysts See Gold in Oversold Territory
data.description:
International gold and silver futures rose sharply on the 27th, extending their recent rebound amid a weaker U.S. dollar, recovering physical gold demand and improving global equity sentiment. According to Odaily, trading activity eased after the U.S. holiday, reducing some of the pressure that recent stock-market selling had placed on precious metals. December gold futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange reached $3,650 an ounce, with gains at one point exceeding 3%; December silver futures stood at $43.50 an ounce, after rising more than 8% at one point.

Analysts said gold had rebounded strongly from a 15-month low, supported by selling fatigue and positive seasonal factors, but cautioned that it was too early to declare a market bottom. Several investment banks and market analysts consider gold to be in oversold territory, but said that does not constitute a buy signal and that oversold conditions could last longer than investors expect.

data.title: STOCKS | ARK Invest Bought More Than 70,000 SpaceX Shares, Cut Shopify and Illumina Holdings
data.description: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest adjusted its holdings on November 27, buying more than 70,000 shares of SpaceX and reducing its positions in Shopify and Illumina. According to Odaily, trading records disclosed by Ark Invest Tracker show that ARKK bought 70,601 shares of SpaceX (SPCX), 24,873 of Twist Bioscience (TWST), 35,772 of CRISPR Therapeutics (CRSP), 115,086 of Recursion Pharmaceuticals (RXRX), 10,114 of Tempus AI (TEM), 1,857 of Natera (NTRA) and 8,213 of Beam Therapeutics (BEAM). ARKK sold 39,123 shares of Shopify (SHOP) and 93,123 of Illumina (ILMN), while ARKQ sold 296 shares of BYD (BYDDY).

data.title: Lee Jae-myung Says South Korea Will Mobilize All Resources to Become a Global AI Leader
data.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae-myung attended the groundbreaking ceremony for the GS artificial intelligence data center in Donghae, Gangwon Province. According to Odaily, he said governments are competing globally over AI technology and South Korea would mobilize all resources to become a leading AI nation that sets global standards and guides development. He added that gaining an early lead in the AI race could change the competitive landscape.

Lee said Gangwon Province would develop into a key base for South Korea’s AI industry. The data center is expected to become one of Asia’s largest AI infrastructure projects and attract investment from global companies. He said the government would support industries involved in the center’s construction and operation, including construction, electricity, energy and cooling, with the goal of benefiting local businesses and talent.

data.title: Analyst Says Customers May Get Only Half of Needed DRAM in 2026; Micron’s 2027 Supply Reportedly Sold Out
data.description:
Citrini analyst Jukan posted on X about a Nikkei interview with Micron Japan. According to Odaily, the interview indicated that customers would receive only about half the DRAM they need in 2026, while Micron’s 2027 supply has reportedly sold out.

Micron expects DRAM supply to be tighter in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026. The company plans to begin moving equipment into its new Hiroshima wafer fab in the second half of 2028, then raise production capacity in stages.

data.title: Richard Teng Says Future Finance Users Will Prioritize Financial Access
data.description: Binance announced on X that co-CEO Richard Teng said the next generation of users entering the digital economy will not necessarily identify as crypto users or care whether their money is onchain. He said they will prioritize getting paid, protecting their savings and investing in opportunities.

data.title: SafePal Says Repaired System Had No Remaining Vulnerabilities After August Security Incident Involving Order Data
data.description:
SafePal said its affected system had no remaining vulnerabilities after repairs were completed in August. According to Odaily, the security incident disclosed that month also involved some previously unidentified order information, including names, email addresses, countries, order numbers, products purchased and payment IDs.

The incident did not involve shipping addresses, phone numbers, wallet accounts, payment addresses, bank cards or bank account information. An independent audit confirmed the system had no vulnerabilities after the August repairs. SafePal said users’ seed phrases and private keys were unaffected and that it would never ask users to provide them. The company urged users to watch for phishing emails or letters posing as communications about firmware updates or device replacements.

data.title: Hong Kong Stock-Related Contracts Rise Broadly in 24 Hours
data.description: Hong Kong stock-related contracts rose over 24 hours. According to Odaily, Zhongji Innolight gained 9.6% to 78.53 USDT, while HK1888 rose 6.0% to 24.4 USDT.

data.title: Richard Teng Opens Binance Blockchain Week in Bangkok
data.description: Binance Blockchain Week opened in Bangkok with a keynote from Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng, who outlined how crypto, traditional finance, and digital infrastructure are increasingly converging into what he described as the next generation of finance.Speaking to an audience of builders, founders, investors, regulators, and users, Teng said the industry is moving beyond a phase where crypto is treated as a standalone category. Instead, blockchain-based tools are becoming part of how people get paid, save, invest, and access global opportunities.“The next generation of users entering our digital economy industry will not necessarily think of themselves as crypto users,” Teng said. “They won't care whether the asset is on-chain… but what they will care about is this: Can I get paid? Can I protect my savings? Can I invest in opportunities beyond [their home market]? And can I partake in global opportunities?”That shift in user expectations was central to his message. Rather than framing crypto as a niche sector, Teng argued that the industry is evolving into broader financial infrastructure centered on utility, access, and trust.Crypto and Traditional Finance Are Moving CloserA key theme of Teng’s speech was the growing overlap between blockchain-based finance and traditional markets. He said the pattern mirrors the evolution of the internet, which first connected information, then people, and finally value.“Crypto is no longer a side rail,” he said. Stablecoins, he noted, are becoming part of payment rails, while tokenized assets are increasingly entering financial portfolios. He added that institutions are no longer waiting on the sidelines. “Institutions are now building in this landscape instead of waiting at the sideline,” he said.Among the clearest examples of this shift, Teng pointed to tokenized equities, which he described as a fast-growing area. For users who have historically faced barriers to international investing — including access to U.S. equities and other global markets — tokenized assets can open new pathways to participation.He stressed that the opportunity is not simply to place existing assets on-chain, but to rethink how they are accessed, distributed, traded, settled, and used. In his view, blockchain infrastructure can make financial markets more global, more continuous, and more flexible through fractional access and programmability.Traditional markets remain powerful, Teng said, but they are still shaped by geography and trading-hour limitations. Against that backdrop, he described Binance as “evolving from a crypto exchange into a 24/7 multi-asset class platform,” where crypto remains the foundation while users can also access stablecoins, payments, tokenized assets, ETFs, equities, and more through a single account.Trust, Security, and Regulation as the FoundationTeng also emphasized that innovation on its own is not enough. “The future of finance cannot be built on innovation alone,” he said. “It must also be built on trust.”He said trust is earned through action, especially during moments of stress. Referring to a recent coordinated security incident affecting the industry, Teng said Binance moved quickly to protect users, set aside sufficient funds, and cover losses in full. According to his remarks, 95% of impacted assets were replenished within two days, and all have since been restored.He added that users could verify holdings through proof of reserves, and said Binance published a report on the incident so the wider industry could learn from it. Teng also noted that Binance engaged external security firms Mandiant, SlowMist, and Verichains for audit and review.“The true test of any financial institution is how it reacts under pressure, what it does to protect consumers, how it pushes for transparency, how it rebuilds and become stronger,” he said.Teng then broadened the discussion to the changing security environment shaped by AI. He warned that fake recruiters, fake interviews, fake companies, and increasingly realistic digital impersonation are expanding the attack surface for all organizations, not just crypto firms. As a result, he said, companies will need to treat AI infrastructure as part of their critical infrastructure going forward.He also pointed to the role of stablecoin issuers during the recent incident, saying they froze more than $2 billion in stolen funds, in some cases within minutes. In his view, that showed how blockchain infrastructure can work alongside regulatory frameworks to enable real-time response, cross-border coordination, and enforcement.Asia’s Role in the Next Financial ChapterTeng used the Bangkok stage to highlight Asia’s importance in shaping the future of finance. He said Binance brought Blockchain Week back to Asia because the region is where “the old meets the new, where tradition meets innovation.”He described Asia as not only one of the world’s most active crypto regions, but also a place where workable models are emerging under clearer rules. Across Asia-Pacific, jurisdictions are moving at different speeds, but they are generating practical lessons on infrastructure, innovation, oversight, and consumer protection.For Teng, this is why regulation should be viewed as an enabler rather than an obstacle. “Regulation is not a constrain for this industry, it’s a bridge to scale,” he said. In his view, policy clarity brings institutions into the market, and institutions help expand access for the next generation of users.He tied that point to the real-world use of stablecoins, noting that they are increasingly becoming part of the global settlement layer not only for traders, but also for freelancers receiving income, small businesses making cross-border payments, and families sending money overseas. These are use cases, he suggested, that address financial needs traditional systems have often failed to serve efficiently.In closing, Teng said the next generation of users will not want separate services for banking, payments, transfers, and investing. They will want a more unified financial experience. Binance’s role, he said, is not to replace traditional finance, but to help build an environment “where finance, all finance, lives on Binance” — one that is open, flexible, interoperable, and designed around user needs.His keynote set the tone for Binance Blockchain Week in Bangkok with a clear message: the future of finance will be shaped by the convergence of crypto and traditional markets, supported by trust, regulatory clarity, and broader global access.
